subject: Airlock transfer & patch sign-off: technical acceptance questionnaire
messages:
From: Anika Shah <anika.shah@stellarishealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procure@stellarishealth.com
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial questionnaire: airlock transfer + patch sign-off expectations

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement we need to validate operational controls for on-prem/private deployments. Two discrete areas our infra/security team asked for details on: (1) airlock (sneakernet/scoped transfer) process for model bundles/patches into sealed environments, and (2) offline patch signing / integrity verification you expect customers to follow.

Could you provide a short technical questionnaire or set of acceptance criteria we can include in our SOW and security review? Specific items we care about: checksum/hash algorithms supported, recommended HSM signing flows, operator separation (who signs vs who applies), offline verification tooling, and what logs/evidence Redwood can provide post-transfer.

Our timeline is tight — procurement would like the answers by end of week so we can finalize an addendum.

Thanks,

Anika Shah
Senior Security Engineer
Stellaris Health

Subject: Re: Initial questionnaire: airlock transfer + patch sign-off expectations

Anika —

Appreciate the clear asks. I put together a short questionnaire and a template sign-off sheet that matches how we operate with other regulated customers; attaching the spec and the template. High-level answers up front:

- Checksums: we recommend SHA-256 for all transfer artifacts; we also support SHA-512 if you want longer digests.
- Signing: customer-managed HSM (PKCS#11) recommended for offline signing; we support verification against ECDSA P-256 and RSA-2048 public keys.
- Operator separation: endorse two-person rule — one operator signs, a distinct operator applies. The template has fields for signer and applier and an evidence checklist.
- Verification tooling: we provide a CLI verifier that validates digest and signature against embedded manifest; it runs without network dependencies and produces an auditable JSON report.
- Evidence telemetry: post-transfer we can emit an attest file (signed by Redwood runtime) that includes time, artifact digest, installer checksum, operator IDs (if configured), and a runbook reference. We can also provide a signed statement of validation if you require a formal attestation.

See attached: airlock_transfer_spec.pdf and patch_signoff_template.xlsx. Monica — can you review the HSM flow diagram and add any operational notes? Marissa — flagging for potential SOW language we can offer.

Rafael
Director, Product Engineering — Redwood Inference

Attachments: airlock_transfer_spec.pdf, patch_signoff_template.xlsx
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial questionnaire: airlock transfer + patch sign-off expectations

Anika / Rafael —

Quick operational clarifications after reviewing the spec and internal HSM notes:

1) Key formats: our offline signer accepts PKCS#11 HSM tokens and also PEM-encoded private keys (for air-gapped customers only when HSM is not available).
2) Signing algorithms: default ECDSA P-256; for clients requiring RSA we support RSA-2048.
3) Offline workflow (short):
   - On builder host (non-airgapped): produce artifact.tar.gz, generate SHA-256 digest, create manifest.json, sign manifest with HSM key -> manifest.sig.
   - Transfer via airlock media (USB or secure courier) to isolated site.
   - Operator at site runs redwood-verify --manifest manifest.json --sig manifest.sig which validates digest + signature and writes verification_report.json.
4) Evidence retention: verification_report.json is time-stamped and can be pushed to your internal SIEM; Redwood can optionally produce a secondary signed attestation file (.attest) we host in an S3-backed evidence bucket for a configurable retention period (default 90 days).

Attached: hsm_keyflow.png (simple flow diagram). Rafael — one question: do we want to include an optional PKI cross-cert step in the template for customers who require CA-based chain verification?

Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: hsm_keyflow.png
From: Anika Shah <anika.shah@stellarishealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 24 May 2028 10:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial questionnaire: airlock transfer + patch sign-off expectations

Thanks Monica — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our security team:

- Can your verifier produce a signed verification_report (i.e., Redwood runtime signs the JSON with a distinct Redwood key) so we have vendor-signed evidence in our artifact store?
- For the two-person rule, does the verifier capture operator identities via PKI client certs, or are you relying on manual name entry in the template? We prefer machine-attested operator IDs where possible.
- For customers that cannot use HSMs, the option to use PEM keys is acceptable but our policy requires the private key to be stored on an offline, encrypted medium. Can you state any recommended key protection guidance in the template?

Procurement side: will the signed attestation (.attest) be accessible to us (read-only) or only Redwood-managed? We prefer read-only access for archival.

Thanks — if you can answer those three items we should have enough to update our SOW and move to signature.

Anika

Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial questionnaire: airlock transfer + patch sign-off expectations

Anika —

Answers inline:

1) Signed verification_report: yes — our verifier can produce a vendor-signed verification_report.json and an accompanying verification_report.sig. The report is signed by a Redwood verification key (separate from runtime keys) and we can publish the verification public key or provide an X.509 leaf for your validation.

2) Operator identity capture: the verifier supports two modes:
   - PKI mode: operator presents an X.509 client cert to the verifier (no network required if certs and CRLs are pre-provisioned) and the cert subject is recorded in the report.
   - Manual mode: operator logs name/email during sign-off; template stores that entry. We recommend PKI client certs for audit integrity.

3) PEM-only customers: we include guidance in the template recommending storing private keys on an encrypted, tamper-evident medium (FIPS 140-2 L2 hardware tokens or encrypted USB with secure passphrase). We also suggest using an HSM where possible; the template calls out minimum crypto policies (disable weak ciphers, rotate keys annually, protect private key with passphrase and physical control).

4) Attestation access: we can provide read-only access to the signed attestation (.attest) via a customer-controlled S3 bucket or via a signed, time-limited URL. By default Redwood will retain the attestation for 90 days, but we can extend retention or export on a schedule per SOW.

Next steps (proposed timeline):
- Rafael/Monica: finalize the template with the PKI cross-cert paragraph and add recommended key storage wording (today).
- Anika: review updates and confirm if PKI is acceptable or if you want PEM-only fallback (end of Monday).
- Procurement: finalize SOW addendum referencing DL-2028-0731 and the attached template (mid next week).

Marissa — approve adding the PKI cross-cert language and the 90-day attestation default? If so I will send a redlined SOW paragraph for procurement.

Thanks all,

Rafael Mendes
Director, Product Engineering — Redwood Inference
